subject.title: feat(gateway): wire coding tools into /tools/invoke HTTP surface

question: Should owner-authenticated Gateway direct invoke support built-in `write` and `edit` behind `hostFsWrite`, an explicit per-tool allowlist entry, and `senderIsOwner === true`?
rationale: The patch deliberately makes remote direct invocation capable of mutating the Gateway host filesystem; tests establish enforcement but cannot choose that product security boundary.

options.title: Accept triple-gated writes
options.body: Keep read, write, and edit behind separate class opt-ins, per-tool allows, and owner/admin identity, with the documented audit warnings.

options.title: Land read only
options.body: Remove `hostFsWrite` and write/edit materialization while retaining the lower-risk read-only path.

options.title: Keep coding tools unavailable
options.body: Reject direct invocation of built-in host-filesystem tools and leave the broader request unresolved.

recommendation.title: Accept triple-gated writes
recommendation.body: Keep read, write, and edit behind separate class opt-ins, per-tool allows, and owner/admin identity, with the documented audit warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository history ties this person most directly to the existing owner-only HTTP tool-invoke authorization boundary.
